root_idea.summary: The core orientation is perishing: something is brought to ruin, extinction, or an end.
root_idea.development: The desert term بيداء is connected with a wilderness that destroys or exhausts those who enter it. The particle بيدَ meaning “other than” is treated as divergent from this core, possibly constituting an independent origin.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form بَادَ rather than the inflected Quranic form تَبِيدَ.

senses.definition: To perish, pass away, become extinct, or come to an end.
senses.usage_conditions: Form I intransitive verb; in the supplied Quran occurrence, it describes something that may perish or cease to exist.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use referring specifically to the sun’s setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause to perish; to destroy or annihilate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative verb, commonly transitive with the destroyed person or thing as its object.
An inseparable particle used before أَنَّ and its complement, normally in the accusative and in an exceptive construction.
A reported alternative analysis of the particle in a traditional saying; this interpretation is disputed in the supplied evidence.
A reported interpretation in an explanatory construction; other authorities analyze the same usage as meaning “other than” or “except that.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert or waterless open tract; a level expanse with little or no vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote a broad, plain, rugged, or otherwise barren tract of desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-ass, especially a wild or desert-dwelling she-ass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also treated by some authorities as an epithet rather than a substantive animal-name; its derivation is disputed.

cautions: The particle بَيْدَ has disputed Classical Arabic analyses: “other than/except that” is distinguished from reported interpretations “on/upon” and “because of.”
